text:
devon: heads-up — latency burn rate on /generate-route just spiked, >2x SLO for the last 5m. seeing a lot of kernel-fallbacks + KV miss rate creeping up :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Pager fired: latency-burnrate:/generate-route. paging @sophia @kevin @maria :phone:
sophia: pulling traces now. p50 ok, p95->p99 jumping. token-level breakdown points to kernel dispatch time and KV lookup tail contributing most of the extra ms.
kevin: did we push any kernel changes recently? I rolled kernel-v2.3 as a canary ~02:10 UTC for better fp16 kernels and new matmul kernels.
devon: yeah that canary + the batching tweak to increase opportunistic batch windows may be interacting poorly for short-req workloads. we saw similar head-of-line earlier in dev.
maria: grabbing profiler snapshot and a KV timeline. here's the quick query I'm running in datadog:```
avg:inference.token_latency_ms{route:generate}.rollup(avg,60) by {stage,kernel}
avg:inference.kv_lookup_ms{route:generate}.rollup(p50,60)
```
infra-bot: KV cache alarm: miss_rate=0.18 (threshold 0.12) for shards a3-c1, a3-c2.
sophia: profiler flame shows kernel-v2.3 path invoking remote HBM path for certain kv ids — remote fetches are adding ~6-12ms tail. also batch sizes on those shards jumped to 120-128 briefly (config change?)
kevin: remote-config change went out with canary: max_batch_size=128 default for gpu-pool-fast. that was intended for throughput, but for the /generate-route which has many short seqs it worsens latency.
devon: immediate mitigation plan (short):
- rollback kernel-v2.3 canary for affected shards
- set max_batch_size back to 64 for route /generate-route via rollout config
- enable KV prefetch/warmup for hot prefixes on that route
- temporarily relax anomaly detector so pages are not spammed while we stabilize
kevin: oncall — can you execute rollback + batch-size override? I can stage the KV warmup script and a rollback playbook.
oncall-bot: executing rollback: pin kernel=kernel-v2.2 for route=/generate-route on shards a3-c1,a3-c2. job 0x9f21 queued. ETA ~30s
sophia: I started a temporary dashboard snapshot (Console -> Dashboards -> snapshots -> share) with token-level breakdown (kernel dispatch / kv lookup / attention / tokenization). Sharing link in thread.
maria: running profiler diff between v2.2 and v2.3 canary now, will post flamegraphs. initial snapshot shows +9ms tail in kv lookup path on v2.3.
oncall-bot: rollback completed on a3-c1,a3-c2 — kernel pinned to kernel-v2.2. system reported degraded=0, fallback-events down to baseline.
devon: nice. can we also add a per-route token-level SLO (p95 token-latency) so burn-rate alert triggers earlier for routes that are sensitive to kernel selection? current alert is per-cluster aggregate and hides route-specific issues.
kevin: yes — we'll add route-level metrics and a small anomaly-detector tuned to token-breakdown deltas (KV lookup + dispatch). will followup with a small PR to alerts repo.
sophia: low-friction followups:
- add a heatmap dashboard of batch-size distribution per shard
- instrumentation: tag traces with selected-kernel and kv-path (local|remote|fallback)
- alerting: create burn-rate policy that pages at 1.5x for route-level p95 for 5m with auto-mitigations documented
maria: noted. I'll attach profiler outputs and file a short postmortem doc for eng-runtime that includes playbook steps and the config diffs.
devon: tl;dr: rollback fixed immediate spike. root cause likely interaction between canary kernel selection + aggressive batch-size config causing KV path to go remote for some ids. followups assigned. :thumbsup:
